summary: Feature: the sketch origin and the H and V axes are fixed elements that every sketch relation can name, as the point @origin and the lines @h and @v. They are never stored, and the @ prefix is reserved: a stored point, edge or relation id that starts with @ is refused. Relations reach them through their operand signatures, as any other point or line: Coincident places a point at the origin or on an axis, Midpoint keeps the origin at the middle of a line, Parallel, Perpendicular and Collinear take an axis as a line, Symmetric mirrors about an axis, Distance, the point-to-line distance and Angle measure from the origin or an axis, a new Tangent keeps an arc or circle touching an axis on the side it is on, and Concentric and Coincident centre an arc or circle on the origin or keep the origin on one. What an axis lacks is a capability, so Equal, a line and arc Tangent and Midpoint on an axis, and Fix on the origin, are refused with the reason, and a relation whose operands are all fixed is refused. A condition another kind already keeps is stored only in that kind, its canonical form: a point at the origin, on an axis, or level or upright with the origin is a fixed coordinate at 0, a line parallel or perpendicular to an axis is Horizontal or Vertical, a line collinear with an axis holds both ends at 0, and a distance from an axis or along one from the origin is a signed fixed coordinate. The planner plans that form and recognises it as already applied, and a parse refuses the other form, naming the one to store. The lowering gives the fixed coordinates as sentinels: an equation on them takes a simpler form where one exists, and otherwise their values become fixed parameters made once, through the lowering context, which refuses what an axis cannot give with its typed refusal. The datum special cases are deleted: the datum pick type, datum-only planning, the datum labels and glyph naming, and the panel's position-from-the-origin command, which the Dimension tool replaces. The canvas still draws the axes and the origin; picking one gives an ordinary selection that the selection set, the relations panel, highlights, snaps and agents share, labelled Origin, H axis and V axis. A point and the origin take a Distance, or a horizontal or vertical distance that holds the point's coordinate; a line takes its angle to an axis and its distance from the origin; Mirror copy may mirror about an axis.
warning: Potentially breaking for CAD files and agents, none for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions or controller output. The sketch graph reserves ids starting with @: a sketch that stores such a point, edge or relation id no longer opens (reserved-sketch-id). A relation is non-canonical only when it names @origin, @h or @v, so every relation a sketch stores today keeps its meaning; a relation submitted with one of them in a form another kind keeps is refused (non-canonical-sketch-relation), naming the form to submit. Relation, selection and mirror operands now accept @origin, @h and @v; agents that relied on a selection set or a mirror refusing them get them accepted, and edits that would move, trim, delete, convert, offset or copy them are refused (fixed-sketch-element). The CAD format is alpha and carries no compatibility either way, so sketches saved by this release that name the origin or an axis do not open in older releases. The equation baseline of 0.0.788 is unchanged: every sketch that names neither compiles to the same equations, byte for byte. The worker protocol version stays 7.

checklist.schema: Sketch graph schema change: ids starting with @ are reserved (reserved-sketch-id), and relation operands may name the virtual @origin, @h and @v, validated by CAD_SKETCH_ELEMENT_ID_PATTERN. A new tangent relation kind keeps an arc or circle touching an axis. Relations on the origin or an axis that another kind keeps must be stored in that canonical form (non-canonical-sketch-relation); relations whose operands are all fixed are refused (fixed-sketch-relation); an axis's missing length, ends or middle is refused (unsupported-sketch-operand). No UPID, post, machine package, execution plan, saved revision, storage, journal, worker reply or native buffer protocol schema change. The native protocol stays version 7 with the same buffers, and the Rust solver and the committed WebAssembly module are unchanged. Post engine API remains 1 and saved-job engine remains 3.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Agent operand change: set-sketch-relation, select-sketch-geometry-set and mirror-sketch-geometry accept @origin, @h and @v where a point or line operand is taken; the edits that change named geometry refuse them with fixed-sketch-element. Looking an id up as the origin or an axis is a comparison with three constants, so it costs the same for any sketch size. Nothing new runs on pointer moves: the canvas already hit-tested and drew the origin and axes, and they now carry their ids instead of datum names. The planner's coordinate trace treats the axes as two more lines in its existing index, built once per graph.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change, and no WebMCP tool added or removed. The set-sketch-relation edit description names the virtual operands and the canonical rule; the WebMCP discovery metadata stays within its 51,200-byte budget at 51,194 bytes, after tightening the element id pattern and the viewport description. The public agent guide documents the operands, the canonical forms, the refusals and the mirror about an axis. Constrain lists a disabled row with its reason for what an axis or the origin cannot take, and the relation list, marks, snaps and highlights name the H axis, the V axis and the origin.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Saved CAD documents parse with the stricter sketch rules above; nothing is rewritten.

publicNotes.summary: The sketch origin and the H and V axes work in every sketch relation.
changes: Pick the origin or an axis with sketch geometry for Coincident, Midpoint, Parallel, Perpendicular, Collinear, Symmetric, Concentric and Tangent, as with any point or line.
Dimension measures a point from the origin as a distance, a line's angle to an axis and a line's distance from the origin.
Mirror copy can mirror about the H or V axis.
Constrain shows what an axis or the origin cannot take, with the reason.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions and controller output are unchanged. Sketches that name the origin or an axis do not open in older releases.
